memo: 41-year-old with valid SNAP/TANF work-requirement compliance via county employment program (60h/mo). Screening flags exemption: snap_tanf_compliance. Per EX-ALIGN, a person meeting SNAP or TANF work rules is deemed compliant with Medicaid — one set of rules, not two. Proof required is SNAP or TANF case number; member has program_enrollment_letter. Deadline is 2026-08-06 (20 days away, not breached). Although hours are currently 20 short of 80/month, the exemption path—confirmed by case number—makes hour makeup unnecessary. Recommend submitting SNAP/TANF case number as primary response; member should keep program letter handy for state verification reference. No escalation needed if case number is available.
member_impact: Good news: you are already meeting Medicaid's work requirement. Because you are complying with SNAP's work requirement through the county employment program, you are automatically deemed compliant for Medicaid too. You only have to follow one set of rules, not two. All you need to do is provide your SNAP case number in your response. Your program letter shows what you are doing, so keep that. You have until August 6, 2026 to respond.
recommended_actions: Locate your SNAP or TANF case number (on your last SNAP letter or EBT card).
In your response to the Medicaid notice, state your SNAP/TANF case number and reference your participation in the county employment program.
Attach or reference the program_enrollment_letter you have on hand as supporting evidence.

citations.quote: A person who is complying with the work requirements of SNAP or TANF is deemed to comply with the Medicaid requirement — one set of rules, not two. The SNAP or TANF case number is sufficient for the state to confirm by data match.
Adults age 19 to 64 covered through Medicaid expansion must complete at least 80 hours per month of qualifying activities, unless an exemption applies.
